newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-TIRED NORMAN BOWS OUT TO STEVEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TIRED NORMAN BOWS OUT TO STEVEN.

text.p: Tired Magnus Norman failed to build on Saturday's impressive Wimbledon victory over Goran Ivanisevic, bowing out in four sets against New Zealand's Brett Steven on Sunday.
Steven won 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 6-3 6-1 and in the third round will now face Frenchman Cedric Pioline who knocked out number 15 seed Wayne Ferreira in straight sets.
Norman needed courtside treatment for a racing heartbeat in Saturday's marathon clash with big-hitting Ivanisevic.
But the Swede said it was tiredness rather than his heart which was to blame for his sluggish performance.
"The heart didn't affect it (his performance), but the length of the match did," he said.
Norman could not reach his Swedish doctor last night, but after seeking advice from a British doctor was convinced there would be no danger to his health if he played.
"I didn't feel very good but I took the decision to play because the doctor said it was not dangerous," Norman said. "But of course I did think about it."
Steven lost the first set in a tie-break, but looked the stronger and fitter.
His gutsy returns of Norman's powerful serve and skilful placing of long balls drew gasps from the crowd.
Steven was pleasantly surprised by his own performance but conceded that his opponent may not have offered his best.
"I played well in the last three sets, but I could see he was tired, especially after that long match with Ivanisevic," he said.
Playing on court five, just outside centre court, both players had to contend with a Wembley-type atmosphere from Briton Tim Henman's nail-biting match against Paul Haarhuis.
"It was very difficult to concentrate. I felt like I was at a soccer match," said Steven.
